summary.oneLiner: A steady, is funding growth with refinance/CASA rather than costly bulk deposits

one-line thesis: A steady, guidance-beating quarter from a fast-growing mid-cap PSU: business +19% and advances +27% YoY (both above guidance), asset quality held at March levels (GNPA 1.45%, NNPA 0.13%, PCR 98.55%) and profitability strong (OP +21%, PAT +27%, ROA 1.9%, ROE 24.65%). NIM slipped 10 bps to 3.85% on MCLR-reset drag but still 10 bps above the 3.75% guide. Management **explicitly refused to raise the 18% loan-growth guidance** despite over-delivering, is funding growth with refinance/CASA rather than costly bulk deposits, and holds a **Board-approved Rs 5,000 cr equity raise** in reserve for the fast credit growth.
financial scorecard (q1fy27, yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total business | +19% (+Rs 1,04,000 cr) | vs 16-17% guide | Beat |
| Total advances | +27% (+Rs 65,000 cr) | vs 18% guide | 3% of growth from IBU; 24% core |
| Total deposits | +13% | vs 14% guide | **No CD raised in Q1** (PSB avg 10-11% ex-CD) |
| CASA | +9% (+Rs 14,000 cr) | | Current-a/c dipped (seasonal Q1) |
| Net interest income | +14.5% | lags advances | NIM compression |
| Operating profit | Rs 3,117 cr (+21%, +Rs 547 cr) | | |
| Net profit | Rs 2,020 cr | +27% | |
| NIM | 3.85% | −10 bps | 10 bps above 3.75% guide |
| ROA / ROE | 1.9% / 24.65% | +10 bps / +165 bps | |
| GNPA / NNPA | 1.45% / 0.13% | held at Mar | vs guides <2% / <0.25%; PCR 98.55% |
| Credit cost | 0.99% | −20 bps | within <1% guide |
| CET1 / CRAR | 15.56% / 18.64% | | well-capitalised |
| Cost of deposits | 4.38% | −22 bps YoY | but **+5 bps QoQ** (retail TD mix) |
| Yield on advances | 8.57% global / 8.66% dom | −71 bps QoQ | MCLR resets from FY26 rate cuts |
> One-offs: treasury income Rs 266 cr (vs Rs 33 cr in Mar-Q) **includes a one-time SR gain of Rs 104 cr**; net worth +Rs 488 cr came from **AFS reserve** revaluation (not P&L). SMA-2 optically jumped Rs 56 cr → Rs 208 cr purely on **one government account of Rs 87 cr** that will regularise.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Loan/advances growth: 18% FY27 — NOT revised up** ("I would not like to relook, revisit our guidance of 18%… we will maintain") despite running at 27%.
- **Total business 16-17%; deposits 14%.**
- **NIM 3.75%** (committed to maintain; expects no further rate cuts, possible hikes → yield support as 53% of book is repo-linked and MCLR base was hiked in recent ALCOs).
- **NII growth 15%.**
- **Asset quality: GNPA <2%, NNPA <0.25%, credit cost <1%, cost-to-income <40%.**
- **Equity raise Rs 5,000 cr this FY** — Board + shareholder + RBI approved; awaiting government approval; will tap at an "opportune time" to fund high credit growth (not dire need — already adequately capitalised).
- **Maharashtra farm debt-waiver expected to conclude within FY27** (see §10).
- **ECL: Rs 2,500 cr total provision needed over 4 years to 31-Mar-2031 (~Rs 125 cr/quarter); ~2 quarters already provided; final norms hit net worth, not P&L** → "ECL does not remain a concern".
- Branch expansion **~200 branches/year** to continue for the next 2-3 years (structural growth driver).
order book & pipeline: N/A (bank). Growth engines: corporate loan book +30% YoY (renewable / data-centre / solar / private capex flagged as bullish focus sectors); **gold loan +75% YoY (+Rs 13,000 cr)**; ECLGS eligible Rs 6,700 cr (sanctioned Rs 4,500 cr, disbursed Rs 3,560 cr — MSME Rs 2,700 cr / corporate Rs 400 cr); new **FCNR 5-yr deposit at 6.60%** to mobilise dollar liquidity (Aug-Sep push expected).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **RAM:Corporate 63:37.** Retail +25%, Agri +30%, MSME +23%, Corporate +30% (corporate accelerated from ~17-18% run-rate).
- **GIFT-City IBU:** book Rs 8,200 cr in ~8-9 months, $965 mn sanctions, ~2-3% of advances; lower NIM than domestic but sticky corporate relationships + ECB cross-sell. Global yield 8.57% vs domestic 8.66% (13 bps drag).
- **Retail underwriting discipline:** no sanctions below CIBIL 681 (subprime cut-off) in 15 months; ~80% of new home-loan sanctions in prime/super-prime (750+).
- **Treasury:** Rs 266 cr Q1 income incl one-time SR Rs 104 cr; upgraded talent hired from other PSBs.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Branch-led deposit mobilisation:** ~200 new branches/yr in scientifically pin-code-selected growth centres; branches breakeven in 2-3 yrs; Rs 21,000 cr of last year's Rs 43,000 cr deposit growth came from **outside Maharashtra**.
- **Digital:** revamped mobile app active users 2.75 lakh → 14 lakh in 9 months (drives stable CASA).
- **FCNR / dollar-deposit window** and **GIFT-City ECB** as new funding/fee avenues.
- **Gold loan** cross-sell into Agri / MSME / retail.
margins & cost dynamics:
- NIM 3.85% (−10 bps YoY): yield on advances fell 71 bps QoQ as MCLR book (44%) resets to prior FY26 rate cuts; **repo-linked book now 53%** → immediate upside if RBI hikes. MCLR base lifted in last two ALCOs → reset tailwind over next year.
- Cost of deposits 4.38% (−22 bps YoY, **+5 bps QoQ** as CASA converts to retail TD; TD growing 16% vs total 13%).
- **Funding strategy:** avoids high-cost bulk deposits; ~Rs 19,000 cr refinance at blended 6-6.5% (no CRR/SLR loading) → CD ratio 87-88% global / 86% domestic / **81.99% including refinance**.
- Opex +8-9% vs 20%+ balance-sheet growth; staff 17,500 (from ~13,000 two years ago); cost-to-income target <40% (running 36-38%).
- Tax rate: OP-basis 12-13%, PBT-basis 16-17% (rural-advance + bad-debt write-off + DTA benefits).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business. "Expansion" = ~200 branches/yr (5-year plan) + tech (mobile app, profitability dashboard for branch/zonal heads).
capital allocation:
- **Rs 5,000 cr equity raise** approved & pending only government nod — a **dilution watch-item** even though CET1 15.56% is comfortable.
- **Provision buffers:** COVID/restructured buffer ~Rs 1,050 cr (≈100% of restructured book, "not really required"), ECL Rs 255 cr already set aside — write-back optionality over coming quarters.
- Growth funded by deposits + refinance, not borrowings ("we are not borrowing and funding").
risks & watch-items:
- **Deposit disintermediation** — management flagged an "irreversible" shift of household savings to SIP/MF/demat (even Tier 2-3), pressuring the core deposit franchise → forces reliance on refinance/CDs/equity.
- **NIM compression** — NII (14.5%) lagging advances (27%); further MCLR resets pending; NIM defence hinges on repo-book re-pricing and no more rate cuts.
- **Maharashtra farm debt-waiver:** eligible book Rs 3,500 cr; govt receivable Rs 2,750 cr; farmer share Rs 260 cr; **max haircut Rs 450-500 cr, but Rs 1,700 cr provision already held + Rs 1,100 cr technical write-off** → net positive to OP via TWO recovery; expected within FY27.
- **Cost of deposits +5 bps QoQ** — CASA converting to TD; question is whether it has bottomed.
- **CD ratio elevated** (global 87-88%) — mitigated by refinance framing (81.99%).
- Segment GNPA up QoQ in retail (housing/vehicle/education) and MSME (small ticket), and one Rs 87 cr government account in SMA-2 (called transient); overall stress still improved (−140 bps YoY to 3.18%).
management quality / tone: Confident, numbers-fluent, disciplined. Repeated "profitable growth, no compromise on asset quality" as the operating mantra; built a branch-level profitability dashboard and is weighting appraisals on profitable growth. Candid on structural deposit-shift and on choosing 18% guidance conservatively. Highlighted governance/ownership traction: FII holding 0.39% → 6.08% and DII 0.24% → 7.42% (ex-LIC) over 2 years.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Over-delivery with a conservative guide is deliberate** — management treats guidance as "sacrosanct" and prefers to beat than chase; 18% held despite 27% actuals.
- **Refinance is the margin lever**, not bulk deposits — 6-6.5% blended, no CRR/SLR, keeps NIM defended while funding 27% loan growth without CDs.
- **Debt-waiver is a net positive, not a hit** — haircut fully pre-provided; TWO recoveries and Rs 50,000/farmer state incentive add SB balances.
- **New-branch "zero-base" effect** structurally inflates growth vs peers — each of ~200 new branches/yr adds incremental business off a zero base.

Guidance held (18% loans, 3.75% NIM, GNPA <2%). Rs 5,000 cr equity raise pending govt nod. Debt-waiver (Rs 3,500 cr eligible) net-neutral-to-positive, expected within FY27. Treasury Rs 266 cr incl Rs 104 cr one-time SR.
